slides.subline: Geu Yetnal Chodang Sundubu — one of around twenty tofu houses in Gangneung's Chodang village, where East Sea water stands in for the coagulant

items.d: Soy milk is set with a magnesium or calcium salt. Fast, consistent, and what most tofu in most countries is made with.

items.t: Chodang tofu — seawater from the East Sea
items.d: The sea is a few minutes' walk from the village. Its minerals do the coagulating instead, which is the whole basis of Chodang's reputation.
Sundubu is the loose curd, eaten before it is pressed. Modubu is the same curd pressed into a block. Most Chodang houses serve both.

slides.title:
The village is
named after
a pen name
slides.body:
Chodang was the pen name of Heo Yeop, a Joseon-era official of the 1500s — the father of Heo Gyun, who wrote The Tale of Hong Gildong, and of the poet Heo Nanseolheon. The story handed down is that he made tofu with the spring water by his office and used seawater in place of brine.

Whether or not one man started it, the method stayed. Roughly twenty tofu restaurants now sit in the few blocks behind Gyeongpo Beach, all working the same way.

What National Geographic recorded at this particular house in June 2026 was owner Lee Young-soon's rule: fresh seawater and good soybeans, and the sundubu is never strained, so it keeps its soft texture.
